paths.title: Beginner path
paths.audience: I am new to ternary computing
paths.description: Build a correct mental model, then write and validate a first TCL function in the browser.

paths.title: Programmer path
paths.audience: I already write systems or application code
paths.description: Trace a program from source through the ISA, VM, compiler, and boot boundary.

paths.title: EECS path
paths.audience: I want implementation and validation evidence
paths.description: Follow the full silicon-to-user path through kernel services, storage, images, and applications.

glossary.definition: A balanced ternary digit with the numeric values -1, 0, or +1.
A positional number system whose digits are negative, neutral, and positive rather than 0 and 1.
The positional base-3 encoding used for scalar arithmetic and numeric values.
A two-bit-per-trit transport encoding used for packed, vector, and tritwise operations.
An operation that combines corresponding trits without interpreting the packed word as a scalar number.
The 27-trit instruction word used by the ISA and stored in 54 meaningful host bits.
A control and status register used for machine, trap, MMU, device, and syscall state.
The .trit source language used by the compiler, kernel, apps, and libraries.
The textual assembly representation emitted by the compiler and consumed by the assembler.
A controlled VM or kernel fault record for illegal, malformed, or otherwise exceptional execution.
A write-ahead log that protects storage updates against interruption and supports recovery.
A repository file, manifest, or test that can verify the claim made by a learning page.
